actorSeparation.note: A defender that has just parried closes on the victim it stunned, and the stun is now the authored 2.47s rather than a compressed 1.75s, so it gets there inside the recording. 0.62 m is the navigation capsules' own contact distance; the scene's lateral offset keeps both actors readable at it.

An attacker's lunge carries it to the navigation capsules' own contact distance now that its wind-up commits later and it no longer re-decides on the way in. 0.6 m is that physical minimum; the scenes' lateral offset keeps both actors readable at it. A swing driven by its own feet stops its forward travel at contact (ENEMY_CONTACT_STOP_DISTANCE) rather than pressing into the player.

groundingLimits.note: Recalibrated after locomotion clips stopped floating. ROLL blends out of a WALK/RUN whose authored vertical COM is now preserved, so the actor enters the tuck from a genuinely lower, correctly-grounded pose and the support solve does more work over the entry frames than it did against a hovering one. The deformed-mesh penetration gate, which is what actually proves the roll stays out of the floor, is unchanged.

motionLimits.note: The tuck roll is the fastest authored motion in the game and the actor is travelling at 10 m/s underneath it. Recalibrated with the grounding limits above, from a known-good rendered roll.

groundingLimits.note: A raised guard is a lower stance than the idle it blends from, and both clips are correctly grounded, so the difference the solver spreads across the blend is real geometry rather than a hover. Same allowance as guard-defense, which is the same interaction with a different thing held. The deformed-mesh penetration gate, which is what actually proves grounding, is unchanged.

A two-handed swing drops its stance further than a one-handed one — the whole reason it reads as heavy — so the blend between the carriage and the swing carries a larger, and real, height difference than the sword chain's. Measured from this passing run; the penetration gate is unchanged. The correction *rate* is allowed the same headroom for the same reason: the stance drop is larger and the swing that causes it is not slower in proportion, so the solve has to cover more ground in a comparable time.
